name: Ophthalmology
description: A precision specialty combining visual science, clinic-based diagnosis, microsurgery, lasers, and long-term patient relationships.

trainingYearsByCountry.usa: 1 preliminary year + 3-year ophthalmology residency (about 4 years total)
trainingYearsByCountry.uk: About 7 years including core ophthalmology and higher specialty training
trainingYearsByCountry.australia: 5-year RANZCO specialist training program after prevocational requirements
trainingYearsByCountry.ireland: About 7 years including basic and higher specialist training

salaryByCountry.australia: A$180k–$350k qualified specialist; A$85k–$118k during training
salaryByCountry.canada: C$220k–$450k qualified specialist; C$61k–$84k during training

salaryLabel: Indicative gross annual range; qualified consultant/specialist first, trainee range second
coreWork: Perform detailed eye examinations and interpret imaging
Manage cataract, glaucoma, retinal, corneal, and inflammatory disease
Use lasers and microsurgical techniques where trained
Explain risk, prognosis, and treatment choices clearly to patients
pathwaySteps: Build a strong foundation in anatomy, optics, and general medicine
Complete ophthalmology rotations, examinations, and surgical logbooks
Develop safe skills in clinics, emergency eye care, lasers, and theatre
Add fellowship training for a subspecialty or advanced surgical practice
goodFit: You enjoy fine detail, visual diagnosis, and delicate technical work
You value measurable improvements in function and quality of life
You want a specialty with a strong outpatient and planned-surgery component
watchOuts: Microsurgical skills require patience and high-volume deliberate practice
Training places can be limited and highly competitive
Emergency eye care still includes time-critical presentations and on-call work

name: Orthopaedic Surgery
description: A hands-on surgical discipline focused on bones, joints, muscles, nerves, trauma, function, and restoring movement.

trainingYearsByCountry.uk: About 8 years including foundation and core surgical training
trainingYearsByCountry.australia: 5-year specialist training program after prevocational requirements
trainingYearsByCountry.germany: About 6 years in orthopaedics and trauma surgery
trainingYearsByCountry.ireland: About 8 years including core and higher specialist training

salaryByCountry.australia: A$220k–$500k qualified specialist; A$85k–$120k during training
salaryByCountry.canada: C$350k–$650k qualified specialist; C$61k–$86k during training

salaryLabel: Indicative gross annual range; qualified consultant/specialist first, trainee range second
coreWork: Assess fractures, degenerative disease, deformity, and sports injuries
Plan and perform open and minimally invasive operations
Use imaging and biomechanics to restore stability and function
Lead rehabilitation planning with physiotherapy and allied health teams
pathwaySteps: Develop broad surgical and emergency skills
Complete orthopaedic rotations, exams, and operative logbook requirements
Build reliable decision-making in trauma, clinics, and operating theatres
Complete fellowship training for a focused subspecialty when desired
goodFit: You like anatomy, mechanics, and visible functional outcomes
You enjoy technical repetition and deliberate practice
You are comfortable with theatre time, acute trauma, and physically demanding days
watchOuts: Training is competitive and operative competency takes sustained practice
Trauma and on-call commitments can be intense
Scope of practice and surgical credentialing are tightly regulated

name: Cardiology
description: A physiology-driven specialty combining longitudinal cardiovascular care with high-stakes diagnostics and advanced procedures.

trainingYearsByCountry.usa: 3-year fellowship after 3-year internal medicine residency (about 6 years post-medical school)
trainingYearsByCountry.australia: About 6 years after medical school: basic + advanced physician training
trainingYearsByCountry.canada: About 6 years: 3 years internal medicine + 3 years cardiology
trainingYearsByCountry.germany: About 6 years in internal medicine and cardiology
trainingYearsByCountry.ireland: About 8 years including core and higher specialist training

salaryByCountry.australia: A$200k–$450k qualified specialist; A$85k–$120k during training
salaryByCountry.canada: C$300k–$550k qualified specialist; C$61k–$86k during training

salaryLabel: Indicative gross annual range; qualified consultant/specialist first, trainee range second
coreWork: Interpret ECG, echocardiography, CT, and MRI findings
Manage acute coronary syndromes, arrhythmias, and heart failure
Perform or assist with catheter-based procedures depending on training
Coordinate multidisciplinary decisions with surgery, emergency, and critical care teams
pathwaySteps: Build a strong internal medicine foundation
Complete cardiology-specific training and logbook requirements
Develop competence in imaging, acute care, and procedural decision-making
Choose a focused subspecialty, research track, or general cardiology practice
goodFit: You enjoy physiology and pattern recognition
You are comfortable making decisions with incomplete information
You want a mix of clinic, ward, emergency, and procedure time
watchOuts: Frequent out-of-hours and emergency work can be demanding
Subspecialty procedures often require additional fellowship time
Licensing, exam, and training eligibility rules vary by country and applicant status

name: Family Medicine
description: A people-centred specialty spanning life stages, preventive care, and the context that shapes a patient's health.

name: Paediatrics
description: Care for infants, children, and adolescents with a blend of acute decision-making and family partnership.

name: Psychiatry
description: A reflective, communication-rich specialty built around mental health, recovery, and the whole person.

name: General Surgery
description: For decisive, hands-on clinicians who thrive in theatre, acute care, and a technically demanding pathway.

name: Radiology
description: A visual and analytical discipline connecting imaging expertise to almost every area of medicine.

name: Anaesthesiology
description: A physiology-first specialty balancing precision, calm under pressure, and procedural confidence.
